overall: Atlanta has run significantly hotter than model guidance today, with the running max already reaching 86.0°F by 17:30 ET — well above all three model forecasts. The warming trend has been steady and uninterrupted throughout the day, and notably, a velocity of +1.8°F/hr is still being recorded at this late afternoon hour, suggesting cooling has not yet firmly set in. The very high dewpoint of 71.6°F reflects a moist, humid airmass that has contributed to an oppressive feel but has not capped the afternoon high as it sometimes does.
forecast_obs_notes: All three models (ECMWF 83.8°F, HRRR 83.9°F, NBM 84.8°F) substantially underforecast today, with the observed running max already exceeding the highest model projection (NBM) by over 1°F as of 17:30 ET. The ensemble signals flagging 83–85°F as the peak range have been entirely invalidated by observed conditions — the day has materially outperformed guidance across the board.
max_temp_prediction: The daily TMAX is locked in at a minimum of 86.0°F, and with velocity still slightly positive at +1.8°F/hr at 17:30 ET, there is a reasonable chance of a marginal additional rise before evening cooling takes hold. However, the flat reading from 17:00 to 17:30 (both 86.0°F) suggests the peak may be very near or already in — a final TMAX of approximately 86.5°F seems most likely, with low probability of reaching 87°F or higher given the late hour. Confidence is high that TMAX finishes above 86°F, and moderate that it holds below 87°F.
